description: A foundational capsule for new consumers, explaining their place, responsibilities, and available stack infrastructure.

declaration.intent: To provide a clear, machine-readable, and human-friendly guide for developers creating a new consumer within the Forge Stack.

scope.summary: This capsule outlines the expected directory structure, integration points with core stack services, and the governance model a consumer must adhere to.

sections.title: 1. Your Place in the Stack
sections.body: As a consumer, you are a self-contained project that lives in the `consumer/` directory. You leverage the core Forge Stack infrastructure for governance, but you have your own mission, roadmap, and ledger. You are a citizen, not a subject.

sections.title: 2. Expected Directory Structure
sections.body: A well-formed consumer should follow this structure to ensure compatibility and discoverability.
sections.code_block:
consumer/
└── your-consumer-name/
    ├── README.md            # Your project's overview
    ├── ROADMAP.md           # Your strategic vision
    ├── ledger.jsonl         # Your consumer-specific audit ledger
    ├── config.json          # Configuration, including stack paths
    ├── src/                 # Your core source code
    └── tests/               # Your tests

sections.title: 3. Available Stack Infrastructure
sections.body: The stack provides the following core services and tools. You are expected to integrate with them, not replicate them. They are your inheritance.

list.definition: The foundation for all knowledge. Use `freeze.py` to create content-addressed IDs and `sign.py` to attest to your capsules. Your own project should be defined by a set of semantic capsules.

The immutable ledger. Use `ledger.py` to create and verify your own `ledger.jsonl`. All significant actions your consumer takes (e.g., creating a new capsule, a major state change) must be pinned to your ledger.
The classification engine. When your consumer makes claims or gathers knowledge, it should be stored in an append-only store and projected into cubes. This separates evidence from judgment.
The trust-scoring mechanism. It operates on DataCubes to produce a lambda (λ) score, quantifying the confidence in a given subject. Your consumer doesn't calculate lambda; it provides the input.
The mechanism for human oversight. For actions with significant consequences, your consumer's egress gates should require a HAL seal from a qualified validator.

sections.title: 4. The Gate Pattern: Your Responsibility
sections.body: You must implement the Gate Pattern (`docs/gate-pattern.md`) to protect your consumer's state and the world from invalid actions. Your ingress gates validate incoming data (e.g., from an LLM or user). Your egress gates validate actions before they cause a world mutation (e.g., writing a file, making an API call).
sections.example: The `CobbleWright` consumer uses an ingress gate to validate AI-generated blueprints before storing them and an egress gate to check for protected player structures before allowing the bot to harvest blocks.

sections.title: 5. Governance and Autonomy
sections.body: Your consumer has its own ledger, anchored to the root ledger. This gives you autonomy. However, you are governed by the stack's protocols. Your `README.md` must include a 'Single-operator disclosure' if you are running in a stack without multiple independent validators, as per the ethical use guidelines.
sections.reference: See `consumer/keystone_gate/README.md` for a reference implementation of a governed consumer.

sections.title: 6. First Steps
steps: Copy this capsule into your consumer's root directory as `onboarding.sc.json`.
Initialize your consumer ledger using `ledger.py genesis --scope your-consumer-name`.
Begin building your core logic, implementing the Gate Pattern for all external interactions.
Define your consumer's core principles and knowledge in its own set of semantic capsules.

validation.self_consistency_check: All paths and tool names are consistent with the root of the `the-full-stack` repository as of 2026-08-10.
